1.1:
Positioning: Which CDP Feature?

Data space layout (recommended): TWO spaces per the use case - a shared RetailOps space for the identity spine + order history (service/ops consumption) and a Marketing space that receives ONLY activation attributes. Rationale: least-privilege - marketing must not read customer purchase history (Phase 11 data-space isolation), while the ops space keeps the order DLOs.

Mechanisms per source:

SourceMechanismWhy
ERP order exports (nightly)Salesforce CSV / file data source + batch mappingBulk, scheduled, fully controlled; freshness is one day - adequate for win-back
Website events (streaming)Streaming API / SDKSub-minute freshness for real-time intent (cart-abandon, momentary churn)
Marketing Cloud sendsMarketing Cloud connectorNative connector brings send/open/click DLOs inbound

Streaming path: the website-events data should be ingested via the Streaming API into a streaming/mapped DLO so a real-time calculated insight and a dynamic segment can drive moment-based journeys (Phases 2, 5, 6).

Expected result: Every source maps to a defensible mechanism; the data-space answer names a boundary with a business justification.

Common mistakes: (1) picking a nightly connector for a real-time moment; (2) putting marketing and ops in ONE space with no boundary; (3) mixing up the MC connector (inbound) with the MCE activation (outbound).
10.1:
Build the Event Subscriber

DataActionEventSubscriberTrigger.trigger:

apex
trigger DataActionEventSubscriberTrigger on Data_Action_Event__e (after insert) {
    if (TriggerHandlerService.shouldRun('DataActionEventSubscriberTrigger')) {
        DataActionHandlerService.handleDataActionEvents(Trigger.new);
    }
}

Test: publish 2 events, then assert exactly 2 Activation_Audit__c (or action-log) rows were created and that the handler never looped DML (bulk: one upsert for the whole event batch).

Batch-hop answer: if the insight is computed on a nightly schedule the alert reacts in days, not minutes. The fix is making the hop streaming (streaming data -> streaming calculated insight -> dynamic segment), not adjusting the report/schedule.

Expected result: exactly 2 audit rows for 2 events; recursion guarded; batch-hop reason articulated.

Common mistakes: (1) subscribing without a recursion guard so a re-insert re-fires the trigger; (2) per-event DML (limits blow up at volume); (3) publishing inside a loop instead of one EventBus.publish(batch).
11.1:
Consent Capture & Suppression

Design (telco self-service):

  • Categories: Email, SMS, Push (and Advertising for marketing use only).
  • Capture sources: web form (opt-in/opt-out per category), call-center agent (records portal + date), API (app settings screen). All writes go through ConsentManagementService.setConsent -> one upsert on Consent_Preference__c. Withdraw-all flips every category to false with source=user portal.

Lab test (ConsentManagementServiceTest):

  1. Capture 3 contacts across 2 categories (contact 1: Email+SMS, contact 2: Email, contact 3: SMS).
  2. Assert consentedContacts(ids, 'Email') returns exactly {1, 2}; consentedContacts(ids, 'SMS') returns {1, 3}.
  3. Withdraw Email from contact 1; re-run - Email returns {2}, and ActivationSyncService.publishActivation now suppresses contact 1 from the Email activation.

Expected result: category-filtered sets correct; withdrawal propagates into the published/suppressed counts.

Common mistakes: (1) storing consent per channel in separate objects so no single view exists; (2) ignoring the source/timestamp fields regulators request; (3) letting an unsubscribe in MC sit only in MC - it must flow back into Data 360 so the next segment honors it.

Field paths to the unified profile: source row -> mapping (field transform + external ID) -> DMO row -> identity-resolution rule evaluates the external ID -> unified UnifiedIndividual record gets the IndividualId. Every activation/segment joins back through that same IndividualId.

Data space decision: this converged customer model belongs in the RetailOps space (it feeds service + analytics). Keep Ad exposure / marketing-purchase combinations OUT of the shared space (Phase 11 least-privilege) so operational users never read marketing-held identity detail.

Expected result: explicit relationship keys (external ID -> IndividualId) and a justified data-space boundary.

4.1:
Match Rule Design

Candidate match attributes: email (deterministic), loyalty ID (deterministic, high confidence = exact), phone (deterministic), name + address (probabilistic/fuzzy). Confidence ratings: unique keys (email, loyalty ID) 0.98+; phone 0.9; name+address fuzzy 0.7-0.85 needs gating.

Rule set to write:

  1. Rule A (deterministic): email equal - high confidence, used by CRM + web identities.
  2. Rule B (deterministic): loyaltyId equal - high confidence, key for order data.
  3. Rule C (deterministic): phone equal - medium-high; safe for service records.
  4. Rule D (probabilistic): name + address fuzzy - ONLY accept when fuzzy score >= 0.85, otherwise keep profiles separate to avoid false merges.

Lab assertion (IdentityResolutionHelperServiceTest): given 4 sample source rows (2 CRM, 1 web visitor, 1 order row), the resolved candidate set size is exactly 3 unique Individuals (the web visitor resolves to the CRM profile via email; the order resolves via loyalty ID; no false merge on fuzzy).

Expected result: matches() returns true for Rule A/B pairs, gates Rule D at 0.85, and the candidate set shows 3 Individuals from 4 sources.

Common mistakes: (1) treating probability as optional - it merges customers when they share a common name; (2) no confidence gating on fuzzy = constant false merges; (3) resolving order data onto the CRM person but not carrying the external key forward to segments.
5.1:
Churn & LTV SQL

LifetimeValue per IndividualId:

sql
SELECT i.IndividualId,
       SUM(o.totalamount) AS LifetimeValue,
       COUNT(o.Id)        AS OrderCount
  FROM UnifiedIndividual i
  LEFT JOIN Order o ON o.IndividualId = i.IndividualId
 GROUP BY i.IndividualId;

Churn proxy (last-order recency):

sql
SELECT i.IndividualId,
       MAX(o.totalamount)                 AS LastOrderDate,
       DATEDIFF(day, MAX(o.totalamount), CURRENT_DATE()) AS RecencyInDays
  FROM UnifiedIndividual i
  LEFT JOIN Order o ON o.IndividualId = i.IndividualId
 GROUP BY i.IndividualId;

Threshold wiring in the lab: CalculatedInsightServiceTest creates 2 members with RecencyInDays > 45 and asserts fireRealTime(...) fires exactly those 2 crossing members (2 action events). Members at or under the threshold fire nothing.

Expected result: LTV grouped correctly; the churn proxy flags recency > 45; the threshold test asserts exactly the crossing members.

Common mistakes: (1) joining the wrong DMO key (must be IndividualId); (2) computing an insight when what is needed is a membership - remember Phase 6, an insight is NOT a segment; (3) forgetting COALESCE for members with no orders (null to 0).
6.1:
Segment Criteria Build

Criteria: Tier = Gold AND OrderCount >= 5 AND RecencyInDays >= 60 in an AND-tree (all three must hold).

Type & refresh decision: for a nightly journey entry this is a static segment refreshed on schedule (daily). It qualifies a fixed list whose membership only changes overnight - no streaming needed. (If the journey had to react within minutes you would downgrade to a dynamic segment.)

Lab math: SegmentMembershipServiceTest feeds 10 candidate rows; exactly 3 match all three criteria. Assert evaluate(criteria).size() == 3 and that the 3 member keys match the expected set (AND logic - a Gold member with OrderCount 2 is excluded).

Expected result: membership list asserted exactly to the 3 qualifying members; the refresh decision is justified against the journey cadence.

Common mistakes: (1) OR-ing the criteria when the brief says all three conditions; (2) choosing dynamic for a nightly batch cadence and over-building; (3) forgetting RecencyInDays >= 60 uses a calendar/date attribute (if you need rolling windows use a calendar segment).
7.1:
Activation Suppression Math

Scenario: 7 members qualify for the segment; 5 carry the Email consent category, 2 do not.

Rule: ActivationSyncService.publishActivation(segment, members, 'Email') runs consentedContacts(members, 'Email') to get the allowed set (5) and publishes only those; the audit records:

FieldValue
Members_Qualified__c7
Members_Sent__c5
Members_Suppressed__c2

Idempotency re-run: run the activation a second time. Because the publish upserts by the member external key (not by a monotonically increasing value), the sent count stays 5 and the audit is updated (Members_Sent stays 5); no duplicate member rows are written.

Expected result: 5 sent, 2 suppressed, audit row persists both numbers, second run is idempotent.

Common mistakes: (1) publishing before suppression (blocked by consent enforcement order); (2) counting suppressed = total minus qualified (wrong, it is qualified minus allowed); (3) letting a retry duplicate member rows because you inserted keyed on a synthetic id instead of the member external key.

MP1:
Consent-Aware Activation Console

ConsentManagementService.setConsent does ONE idempotent upsert:

apex
public with sharing class ConsentManagementService {
    public static void setConsent(Id contactId, String category, Boolean optIn) {
        List<Consent_Preference__c> prefs = [
            SELECT Id, Opt_In__c FROM Consent_Preference__c
            WHERE Person__c = :contactId AND Consent_Category__c = :category
        ];
        Consent_Preference__c p = prefs.isEmpty()
            ? new Consent_Preference__c(Person__c = contactId, Consent_Category__c = category, Opt_In__c = optIn)
            : prefs[0];
        p.Opt_In__c = optIn;
        upsert p;   // one DML; re-capture only updates the same row
    }
    public static Set<Id> consentedContacts(Set<Id> candidates, String category) {
        Set<Id> ok = new Set<Id>();
        for (Consent_Preference__c p : [
            SELECT Person__c FROM Consent_Preference__c
            WHERE Person__c IN :candidates AND Consent_Category__c = :category AND Opt_In__c = true
        ]) { ok.add(p.Person__c); }
        return ok;
    }
}

publishActivation: filter via consentedContacts, publish by external key (idempotent upsert), write the audit (qualified/sent/suppressed). Test: withdraw -> next publish excludes; two runs update rows, never duplicate.

Expected result: L4 numbers proven; re-runs idempotent.

Common mistakes: (1) DML inside the publish loop; (2) suppressing after the send; (3) no audit row.
MP2:
Real-Time Churn Handler

CalculatedInsightService.fireChurnActions:

apex
public static List<Database.SaveResult> fireChurnActions(Set<Id> candidates, Decimal threshold) {
    List<Data_Action_Event__e> events = new List<Data_Action_Event__e>();
    for (Decimal score : churnScores(candidates)) {
        if (score >= threshold) {
            events.add(new Data_Action_Event__e(Member_Key__c = ..., Action_Type__c = 'ChurnAlert'));
        }
    }
    return EventBus.publish(events);   // ONE publish call for all crossings
}

Subscriber: DataActionEventSubscriberTrigger (after insert) delegates to DataActionHandlerService.handleDataActionEvents(Trigger.new), guarded by TriggerHandlerService.shouldRun(...). Handler performs the (simulated) side effect with no DML loop and writes one audit batch.

Test: 50 members, 12 cross the threshold -> exactly 12 events published, exactly 12 audit rows, no DML-loop recorded by the handler.

Expected result: exact counts + recursion guard proven.

Common mistakes: (1) publishing per event (limits blow); (2) no recursion guard so the subscriber re-fires itself; (3) 12 events -> 24 audit rows because you audit both publish and process.
MP3:
Agentforce Grounding Context

apex
@InvocableMethod(label='Get Billing Context')
public static List<String> getBillingContext(List<Request> reqs) {
    List<String> out = new List<String>();
    for (Request r : reqs) {
        if (String.isBlank(r.individualKey)) { out.add(jsonErr('profile-not-found')); continue; }
        out.add(buildContextNode(r.individualKey, r.requestedFields)); // whitelist-only fields
    }
    return out;
}

Whitelist discipline: only fields in the allow-list are emitted; requesting cardLimits returns it OMITTED - the test asserts that an unlisted field never appears in the JSON. Unknown key returns a graceful error node, never an exception to the agent. Callouts guarded via Limits.getCallouts().

Expected result: field whitelist enforced, JSON valid, graceful not-found, callouts guarded.

Common mistakes: (1) returning the whole DMO (context blowup + over-exposure); (2) throwing exceptions the agent interprets as tool failure; (3) no Limits guard on callouts.
